chapter: Dancing schools and Charlie Johnson in New York
title: The dancing school as a learning ground
summary: Playing under Clark, a learned musician, let McRae put his teacher's lessons to work and learn a range of styles.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well after that, that's when I met him -- when I met him, that's why he was playing in the dancing schools, you know. He sent for me and asked if I wanted to work there on 14th Street with him. I said sure. And it was good, because I was a stranger in New York and I was trying to find my way around, you know. I'd take some gigs here and gigs there with different musicians. And when I met June Clark, this was like a learning school. Things you go to school and learn, you know, you put it work. You know, see how much you learned, how much you know and what you can do. Give you a chance to really exercise what you went through with your teacher that taught you. Remember, I went to Atlantic City with

my brothers. This wasn't no strain (inaudible) because this band, everything was just written out for you. And everything we put together, you know, and things like that.
And working in a dancing school, you really had a chance to -- really learn all the music because you --
Especially a guy like June Clark who was a learned musician. He had everything. He make you play organ -- he teach you how to play all kind of (inaudible).
